original_test_intent: Verify the BF3 optical transceiver temperature across IB/OOB SDR, IB/OOB Sensor List and BMC Web, with the sensor bound to the installed module/port and evaluated for identity, description, reading, units, health and freshness against its approved SPEC.
original_method: Prove common target identity, map the BF3 adapter port and installed optical module, record module presence/link/traffic context, collect complete command views and the exact Web row in a bounded interval, then compare normalized fields to transceiver limits without clearing logs or resetting the adapter/link.
manual_activity: A platform/network reviewer approves the BF3 port-to-module-to-sensor mapping and optical-module limits, then confirms the protected Web entry and five-view comparison.
safety_requirements: Do not reset/reconfigure the BF3 adapter, link or module
Bind the sensor to the exact port/module
Exclude BF3 chip and unrelated TRX resources
Capture complete lists and page context
agent_execution_scope: Verify target and BF3 port/module identity
Record presence, link and traffic context
Collect full IB/OOB SDR and Sensor lists
Capture the protected BF3 transceiver Web row
engineer_actions: Approve port/module/sensor map and transceiver SPEC
Resolve absent, swapped or divergent resources

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The OOB `sensor get` is only one required view; its truncated fallback neither supplies IB/Web evidence nor proves which BF3 optical module is measured.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture all four command views and the protected Web entry keyed to verified BF3 port/module identity and current presence/link state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Five interfaces, the BF3 transceiver sensor and timing metadata remain; generic clear and partial evidence are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create one timestamped evidence row keyed by BF3 adapter port and optical-module identity, including presence/link/traffic state, all five views and the applicable module-temperature limit.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds physical module identity and port-state context beyond a generic `grep TRX` match.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A TRX match may belong to another adapter/port or remain stale after module removal, producing a plausible but invalid temperature.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Module labels can differ among NIC firmware, BMC and chassis notation; use the approved port map and inventory identifiers.

project_override_considerations: Define the BF3 port, installed module identity, telemetry source, presence/link behavior, fields, limits and tolerance. BF3 chip telemetry remains independent; private Script use requires pinned review.
expected_evidence: BF3 adapter/port/module inventory and sensor map
Module presence/link/traffic context and approved transceiver SPEC
Complete decoded IB/OOB SDR and Sensor lists
Protected BF3 transceiver Web row and page context
No-BF3/link/SDR/thermal mutation or log-clear audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, procedure and criteria consistently target the BF3 transceiver sensor across five views. Generic log clearing and DeepSeek's partial collection are method defects.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Module identity, port mapping, access and SPEC are identifiable inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED only if the sensor cannot be tied to the installed optical module after those inputs are obtained.

review_improvement: Separates optical-module telemetry from BF3 silicon temperature and requires port/module presence plus complete five-view evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A transceiver sensor describes a removable optical module whose identity and validity depend on the physical port and presence/link state. The BF3 controller can remain healthy while the intended module is absent or another TRX entry is returned, so physical module binding is essential to the acceptance result.
